text:
maria: Heads-up — trying the quickstart sample app on Windows (scoop install redwoodctl v0.9.2) and hitting intermittent login timeouts when running `redwoodctl local serve`. Happens on two different machines.

alex: ugh. can you paste the tail of the logs? is this the interactive device code flow or SSO?

maria: device code flow. UI opens, code shows, I paste it in browser, then redwoodctl hangs at `waiting for login completion` for ~30s and eventually times out. sometimes it succeeds on retry.

sam: @maria do you have a proxy or VPN on? windows credential helper oddities have shown up before with WinHTTP.

maria: no vpn. latest windows updates applied. repro steps: `scoop update && scoop install redwoodctl` then `redwoodctl login --method device` then `redwoodctl local serve --sample quickstart`.

maria: log snippet:
```
INFO 2024-11-02T15:12:10Z redwoodctl::auth Waiting for device flow completion
WARN 2024-11-02T15:12:40Z redwoodctl::http request failed: read tcp 127.0.0.1:52345: i/o timeout
ERROR 2024-11-02T15:12:40Z redwoodctl::auth Device flow timed out after 30s
```

alex: thanks. looks like the http client in the binary might be using a short dial/idle timeout on windows or not honoring system proxy. can you run with `RWD_DEBUG=1 redwoodctl local serve` and paste the full output?

maria: pasted full debug to a gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/abcd1234 — main thing I see is repeated `dial tcp` errors and one `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND` right before success.

sam: that ENOTFOUND smells like flaky DNS on the CI vpn route. but you said no VPN. another possibility: Windows Defender interfering with ephemeral outbound sockets. we had a similar intermittent failure a while back with the installer registering a firewall rule blocking some outgoing ports.

maria: hmm. firewall is default allowed for redwoodctl. I added an inbound rule earlier for localserve but removed it.

alex: can you try `redwoodctl login --method device --timeout 120` to see if it's purely a timing issue? also try `redwoodctl login --method device --no-open` so the browser step is manual — helps narrow if the auto-open short-circuits.

maria: tried `--timeout 120` and it completed 1/3 attempts, failed 2/3. with `--no-open` same pattern.

devex-bot: possible known issue recorded: issue #2145 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ctl/issues/2145) - intermittent WinHTTP deadlines with device flow on certain networks. tagging @devex for triage.

sam: ok leaving a quick checklist: 1) repro on a fresh user profile 2) try `RUST_LOG=trace` to see if tls handshake retries are happening 3) test on non-scoop install (zip binary) to rule out scoop shim.

maria: I can try the zip binary later today and also repro on my personal laptop. if I can reproduce reliably I'll attach network traces.

alex: thanks. filing a minimal follow-up for eng-runtime: probable root is netclient reusing sockets with very short keepalive on windows causing mid-flow read timeouts. will ping infra to add a flaky-win label.

maria: great, appreciate it. will report back with either a clear repro or network traces. :thumbsup:
